visual_anchor: Cranial ultrasound shows echogenic clot at the caudothalamic groove with grade-dependent ventricular filling, dilation, or periventricular hemorrhagic infarction.
rationale: High-frequency neonatal ultrasound diagnosis with a grading scheme and serial visual evolution; not a parent already in the catalog.

visual_anchor: Cranial ultrasound/MRI shows periventricular echogenicity evolving to bilateral posterior periventricular cysts or white-matter volume loss.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: MRI shows symmetric T1 hyperintensity of globus pallidus/subthalamic nuclei; chronic disease may show T2 signal and movement disorder.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Diffuse boggy scalp collection crosses sutures and midline, with subaponeurotic fluid on ultrasound; unlike suture-confined cephalohematoma.
rationale: A high-stakes neonatal scalp finding with strong clinical and ultrasound distinction from existing cephalohematoma.

canonical_name: Physical Child Abuse: Skeletal and Intracranial Imaging
visual_anchor: Skeletal survey demonstrates classic metaphyseal corner/bucket-handle injury or multiple posterior rib fractures; CT/MRI can show abusive head trauma.
rationale: A core recognition topic with high-specificity radiographic injury patterns and clear clinical importance.

visual_anchor: Expiratory/decubitus chest radiograph shows persistent unilateral hyperlucency/air trapping and sometimes contralateral mediastinal shift despite a radiolucent object.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Neonatal radiograph shows dilated small-bowel loops with little or no distal gas and contrast enema reveals unused microcolon; apple-peel variant has a spiral distal bowel around a single vascular pedicle.
rationale: Distinct neonatal obstruction pattern, including the visually memorable apple-peel vascular anatomy; duodenal atresia is a different level and already listed.

visual_anchor: Contrast enema shows a normal-caliber colon with long filling defect from meconium; plug may evacuate during the study.
rationale: Separate imaging diagnosis from existing meconium ileus and Hirschsprung disease, with a recognizable contrast-enema target.

visual_anchor: Contrast enema shows a small descending/sigmoid colon with abrupt caliber transition at the splenic flexure and a normal-caliber rectum.
rationale: A distinct functional neonatal obstruction pattern with a useful contrast-enema sign.

visual_anchor: Ultrasound shows a cyst contiguous with bowel and a layered gut-signature wall (echogenic mucosa over hypoechoic muscle), sometimes a Y sign.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Cross-sectional imaging reveals abnormal organ laterality, interrupted IVC with azygos continuation or anomalous venous return, splenic anomalies, and complex congenital heart anatomy.
rationale: A clinically important multisystem laterality pattern with highly teachable cross-sectional anatomy; comparator Kartagener syndrome is a different disorder.

visual_anchor: Well newborn has blanching erythematous macules/papules with central papules or pustules, mainly trunk and proximal limbs, sparing palms and soles.
rationale: Common one-look benign newborn eruption with practical clinical photo differential; distinct from transient neonatal pustular melanosis.

visual_anchor: A circumferential hair/thread groove with distal swelling and erythema or ischemia of a toe, finger, or penis; the constrictor may be hidden beneath edema.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Coarse facial gestalt, temporal alopecia, pigmentary mosaicism, and hypotonia; mosaic tetrasomy 12p may be missed in blood.
rationale: Distinct face/skin pattern supports visual clinical recognition; mosaicism explains variable phenotype.

visual_anchor: Wide mouth with full lips, deep-set eyes, broad nasal bridge, and characteristic intermittent hyperventilation/apnea in a child with severe developmental delay.
rationale: Distinct facial and episodic breathing phenotype extends the dysmorphology differential alongside separately listed Angelman and Mowat-Wilson syndromes.

visual_anchor: Coronal craniosynostosis with variable hypertelorism, brachydactyly/carpal-tarsal fusion, and hearing loss; CT demonstrates the fused coronal suture.
rationale: A common molecularly defined syndromic craniosynostosis with a recognizable clinical and CT phenotype; other listed craniosynostosis syndromes are distinct.

visual_anchor: Severe symmetric tetraphocomelia or limb reduction with cleft lip/palate, microcephaly, and characteristic facial dysmorphism.
rationale: Distinct limb-reduction and craniofacial pattern; the thalidomide phenotype is an etiologic phenocopy rather than the same disease.

visual_anchor: Postaxial limb-ray deficiency with malar hypoplasia, micrognathia, and cup-shaped ears.
rationale: Distinct postaxial acrofacial pattern; contrasts with the already listed preaxial Nager syndrome.

visual_anchor: Coarse facial appearance, distal nail hypoplasia, and diaphragmatic hernia on prenatal or neonatal imaging.
rationale: Syndromic pattern adds recognizable dysmorphology and nail clues to an existing diaphragmatic hernia topic.

visual_anchor: Prenatal valproate exposure may produce characteristic facial features, metopic ridge, radial-ray defects, and neural-tube defects.
rationale: Etiology-specific teratogenic pattern with visible craniofacial and limb findings; distinct exposure from fetal hydantoin/warfarin syndromes.

visual_anchor: Nasal hypoplasia with stippled epiphyses/vertebrae on skeletal radiographs after first-trimester exposure.
rationale: Distinct radiographic and facial teratogenic pattern; different exposure mechanism from other embryopathies.

visual_anchor: Lateral sacral radiograph shows hemisacrum/sickle-shaped sacrum; MRI/US depicts presacral mass with anorectal malformation.
rationale: Classic triad and recognizable sacral sign distinguish this syndrome from broader caudal regression/sacral agenesis.

visual_anchor: Prenatal/neonatal imaging shows aqueductal stenosis with hydrocephalus; examination shows adducted thumbs.
rationale: Recognizable neurologic and limb combination with a specific neuroimaging anchor.

visual_anchor: Strictly unilateral, sharply demarcated ichthyosiform inflammatory nevus follows Blaschko lines with ipsilateral limb hypoplasia/reduction.
rationale: High-value one-look lateralized skin and limb pattern with disease-specific distribution.

visual_anchor: Large heterogeneous infant CNS mass with possible hemorrhage, cysts, restricted diffusion, and hydrocephalus; posterior-fossa lesions can mimic medulloblastoma.
rationale: Aggressive infant CNS tumor with useful imaging distinctions in a high-stakes medulloblastoma differential.

visual_anchor: In a young child, CT shows a multiseptated cystic or mixed cystic-solid lung mass, sometimes with pneumothorax, in a DICER1 context.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: A rapidly growing infant soft-tissue mass is often heterogeneous and avidly enhancing on MRI, with hemorrhage or necrosis; imaging overlaps vascular tumors and needs pathology correlation.
rationale: Age-specific soft-tissue tumor with a distinctive rapidly growing visible mass and imaging pattern.

visual_anchor: HRCT shows geographic ground-glass opacity centered in right middle lobe and lingula with central/paramediastinal distribution and mosaic air trapping.
rationale: A characteristic pediatric chest CT pattern can suggest diagnosis without biopsy.

canonical_name: Alveolar Capillary Dysplasia with Misalignment of Pulmonary Veins
visual_anchor: Newborn has refractory pulmonary hypertension; chest imaging is nonspecific and confirmation depends on lung biopsy showing reduced alveolar capillaries and misaligned veins.
rationale: The proposed anchor is the lung-biopsy pattern; clinical presentation and radiology are nonspecific, so this is pathology-led rather than a distinctive clinical/radiologic topic.

visual_anchor: Sparse scalp hair, prominent interphalangeal joints, broad fingertips, triangular face, and thick lower lip.
rationale: A named syndrome with a recognizable clinical gestalt or specific radiologic feature makes a useful visual teaching entry.

visual_anchor: Thick flared eyebrows, long eyelashes, downslanting narrow palpebral fissures, and hypertrichosis cubiti (“hairy elbows”).

visual_anchor: Characteristic hypotonic facies with upturned nose, tented upper lip, widely spaced teeth, and genital anomalies; HbH inclusions can support diagnosis.

visual_anchor: Thick hair and eyebrows, downslanting palpebral fissures, open-mouth appearance, joint hypermobility, and later retinal dystrophy.

visual_anchor: Branchial skin defects, ocular coloboma/microphthalmia, and cleft lip or prominent philtral pillars with a broad nasal tip.

visual_anchor: Microtia, patellar hypoplasia/absence, and severe pre- and postnatal growth restriction.

visual_anchor: Craniofacial dysmorphism with microtia/ear canal anomalies, conotruncal cardiac defects, and thymic/CNS abnormalities after exposure.

visual_anchor: Short distal phalanges with punctate epiphyseal calcifications and midface/nasal hypoplasia on radiographs.

visual_anchor: Neonatal seizures with MRI diffusion restriction and evolving cystic encephalomalacia involving cortex and subcortical white matter.
rationale: Distinctive neonatal neuroimaging pattern and course; isolated sulfite oxidase deficiency is a separate existing comparator but can share the imaging differential.

visual_anchor: MRI shows near-complete replacement of cerebral hemispheres by CSF with preserved brainstem and variable falx; distinguish from severe hydrocephalus.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Neonatal diffusion MRI shows restricted diffusion in a unilateral arterial territory, commonly left MCA, with evolving encephalomalacia.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Term neonate with severe respiratory distress and diffuse ground-glass/airspace opacities; imaging is nonspecific.
rationale: Imaging appearances overlap substantially across genetic surfactant disorders; defer separate pages and group gene-specific causes under one pediatric diffuse lung disease entry.

visual_anchor: Diffuse neonatal/infant lung disease with ground-glass opacity and septal thickening on CT; imaging overlaps other surfactant disorders.
rationale: Imaging appearances overlap substantially across genetic surfactant disorders; defer separate pages and group gene-specific causes under one pediatric diffuse lung disease entry.

visual_anchor: Childhood interstitial lung disease with variable ground-glass opacity, septal thickening, and cystic change; CT overlaps other genetic surfactant disorders.
rationale: Imaging appearances overlap substantially across genetic surfactant disorders; defer separate pages and group gene-specific causes under one pediatric diffuse lung disease entry.

visual_anchor: Prenatal ultrasound/MRI shows enlarged echogenic lungs, dilated distal airways, flattened/inverted diaphragm, and fetal hydrops from laryngeal/tracheal obstruction.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: MRI shows a fourth-ventricular/posterior-fossa mass with variable extension through foramina and obstructive hydrocephalus.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Intraventricular tumors are usually lobulated and avidly enhancing; papillomas are frond-like and may cause hydrocephalus, while carcinomas are invasive/heterogeneous and may show necrosis, hemorrhage, or dissemination.
rationale: Use one tumor-family page with clearly separated benign papilloma and malignant carcinoma sections. The two are histologically and clinically distinct, but a shared anatomic site supports side-by-side imaging teaching without treating carcinoma as a papilloma synonym.

visual_anchor: MRI shows a large heterogeneous, invasive, avidly enhancing intraventricular mass with necrosis/hemorrhage and possible dissemination.
rationale: Fold into the proposed Choroid Plexus Tumors page as a separately labeled malignant entity, with its own invasive/heterogeneous imaging pattern and outcome distinction; it is not a synonym of papilloma.

visual_anchor: Ultrasound/CT/MRI shows a large multiloculated cystic or mixed solid-cystic hepatic mass in an infant, often with septa and myxoid stroma.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Renal ultrasound/CT/MRI shows a well-circumscribed multiloculated cystic renal mass with enhancing septa and no solid nodules.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Infant renal mass is large and heterogeneous with necrosis/hemorrhage, often with calcifications and synchronous atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Infant/toddler has a rapidly enlarging soft-tissue mass; MRI shows lobulated fat-containing lesion with septa and variable nonfatty components.

visual_anchor: Rapidly enlarging infant anterior maxillary mass with an expansile lytic lesion and variable spiculated/sunburst bone change on radiographs or CT.

visual_anchor: Ultrasound shows an avascular suprarenal mass that liquefies and shrinks on serial imaging; chronic lesions may calcify.
rationale: Distinct pediatric presentation with a recognizable clinical or imaging pattern and no equivalent topic in the live catalog.

visual_anchor: Small moist beefy-red tissue at the umbilical stump after cord separation, distinguishable from a patent urachus or omphalomesenteric duct.

visual_anchor: Unilateral erythema and swelling of the neonatal breast, sometimes with fluctuance or purulent discharge; ultrasound can identify abscess.

visual_anchor: Recurrent intensely pruritic crops of sterile vesiculopustules favoring palms and soles, often starting in early infancy.

visual_anchor: Unilateral/periflexural papular erythematous eruption begins near an axilla or groin and spreads centrifugally, often becoming bilateral but asymmetric.
